slides.0.title: Northern Corsica
slides.0.subtitle: Patrimonio, Cap Corse, Muscat du Cap Corse and Calvi
slides.1.title: Patrimonio
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Corsica's first AOC
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Founded in 1968 as Corsica's first AOC; limestone-clay slopes behind Saint-Florent
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Nielluccio
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Red and rosé are built on Nielluccio (Sangiovese); the share varies (INAO 90%, WWS 95%); INAO is followed and it is not tested
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vermentino
slides.1.highlights.2.content: White is Vermentino (locally Vermentinu), herbal and citrusy
slides.1.content: The heart of the north.
slides.2.title: Cap Corse
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The peninsula
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A narrow northern peninsula with steep slopes, schist soils and strong sea winds
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Coteaux du Cap Corse
slides.2.highlights.1.content: AOC from 1993; white (Vermentino) leads, with red and rosé also made
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Muscat du Cap Corse
slides.2.highlights.2.content: AOC 1993; a vin doux naturel (VDN) made from Muscat à petits grains blancs
slides.2.content: Sweet and dry whites share the peninsula.
slides.3.title: Calvi and the northwest
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Calvi
slides.3.highlights.0.content: One of the Vin de Corse designations on the northwest coast, on granite and sandy soils
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Style
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Sea breezes add freshness, especially in rosés and whites
slides.3.content: The north offers three geologies and styles.
